relevance_note: Single case report of a girl with Blau syndrome confirmed by NOD2 testing: 'genetic testing showed the NOD2 pathogenic variant c.1000C > T (p.Arg334Trp, abbreviated R334W) missense mutation, which confirmed the diagnosis of Blau syndrome'.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; no tables. Three in-scope people: the proband ('patient', rule 5) and two affected relatives described only in relation to her, labelled by rule 2 as 'mother of patient' and 'maternal half-brother of patient'. The relatives are not stated to have been genetically tested or given a diagnosis, so they have no variant rows and disease_label 'not reported'; the mother is not stated to carry the variant, so inheritance is 'not reported'. The relatives' features are given only as 'similar skin, joint, and eye manifestations' / 'Similar ocular and systemic findings' (recorded as one vague observed feature each, not mapped to specific checklist items) plus 'the mother is legally blind'; 'the half-brother of the patient has an identical phenotype' was not turned into specific features. The patient's retinal vasculitis was not counted toward the checklist item 'vasculitis (large-vessel arteritis, aortitis or leukocytoclastic vasculitis)' because it is none of those types. 'decreased visual acuity' (20/40 each eye) was counted as visual impairment. Zygosity not stated for the patient (only the general statement that the disorder is autosomal dominant). The facial redness/rash was attributed by the authors to adalimumab; recorded as observed features with that detail. Ages: only '5-year-old' at referral/presentation; follow-up of two years without a stated age at last evaluation; no age at onset or diagnosis stated. No contradictions found. HPO IDs given only where confident.
